look_here_first: FIRST LOOK FOR SMALL ROUNDED HEADS, NOT A RED SPOT. Graceful sandmat (Euphorbia hypericifolia) is a GLABROUS upright-to-ascending annual whose tiny cyathia gather in DENSE TERMINAL AND AXILLARY HEADLIKE GLOMERULES with short/reduced bracts. Its opposite oblong leaves are mostly hairless and often finely toothed near the apex. At the nodes look for relatively large reddish TRIANGULAR stipule scales; FNA describes them as joined (connate), generally 1.5–2.2 mm, but the current photos prove their presence/shape better than the precise two-sided fusion seam. Compare E. nutans (leafier loose cyathial clusters, frequently short incurved stem hairs) and E. hyssopifolia (usually less compact/leafier reproductive clusters, smaller stipules). Smooth fruit alone is insufficient because all three may have glabrous fruit. Mature detached seed and definitive scaled smooth capsule macros still needed; nativity-by-county badge is NOT being promoted.

key_traits.label: Family pattern
key_traits.text: Euphorbiaceae; Euphorbia sect. Anisophyllum: opposite unequal leaves, milky latex, cyathium (tiny special flower head), dry three-lobed capsule.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Annual taprooted herb; ascending/erect, 15–50 cm; shoots glabrous. New habit photograph is a potential example, not calibrated proof of height.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Opposite, obliquely oblong to oblanceolate, 10–35 × 7–15 mm, asymmetric base, margins serrate/serrulate especially distally, glabrous; petioles 1–3 mm.

key_traits.label: Stipules
key_traits.text: Paired stipules at nodes fused into deltoid, usually entire scales (occasionally fringed apically), 1.5–2.2 mm, glabrous; often spreading away from stem. Need both-side node photo and scale before arrow labeling exact fusion.

key_traits.label: Inflorescence
key_traits.text: Cyathia crowded in dense, axillary or terminal headlike clusters (glomerules), with much-reduced bractlike leaves, NOT the leafy loosely spaced small cymes of E. nutans or E. hyssopifolia.

key_traits.label: Cyathium
key_traits.text: Four yellow-green/brown, often stipitate glands; white-pink petal-like gland appendages may be inconspicuous or absent from smaller glands. These are not true petals.

key_traits.label: Seed
key_traits.text: About 0.9–1.1 × 0.5 mm; pale brown underneath a thin white mucilage coat; low smooth ridges and shallow irregular pits/depressions, not the 2–3 conspicuous transverse bars often seen in E. hyssopifolia.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: dense terminal and axillary glomerules of many tiny cyathia

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: small, highly reduced bracts at cyathium heads

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: hairless stems and leaf surfaces (verify at basal node, not only at tips)

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: fused triangular nodal stipules about 1.5–2.2 mm

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: asymmetric opposite oblong leaves with finely serrate margins
